answers.reasoning: Continuous torque magnitude is a regression target. Numeric codes can instead denote discrete cluster membership; finite observed targets do not turn the underlying magnitude into a class.
Pairing is by row index. Permuting only X can assign a torque to a different physical example; a shared permutation preserves pairs, while fitting does not infer the lost alignment.
For the explicitly supplied perpendicular static point load, 5*9.8*1=49 N m. Removing mass would give 9.8, not 4.9; 4.9 is a different source training target.

Actual code constructs LinearRegression, fits X_lifting/y_torque, then predicts new_box. Fresh prediction before fitting is invalid; training-row substitution or unmatched feature reversal changes the task.
The graph of y=b0+b1*m+b2*r is one affine plane in three-dimensional input-output space, not a line or an automatically interacting curved surface.
The raw-feature affine model has constant slopes and no m*r term. Product has mixed derivative 9.8; affine mixed derivative is zero. Fixed intercept and summation cannot generate that interaction.
Actual legend shows red training data and yellow new test point. Translucent graph is the fitted plane, not residuals or a confidence interval.

Representative genuinely unseen observations are the strongest test of intended generalization. Training/reused data, duplicated held-out measurements and easier-regime-only samples do not establish deployment performance.
Similar measurement units, sample counts or feature means do not guarantee representative operating conditions or the same input-target relationship.

The stipulated information/capacity deficiency calls for relevant features or adequate representation rather than rerunning converged optimization or changing the split alone. Need check that any capacity wording does not promise to recover genuinely unmeasured information.
Slide places many features relative to examples and excessive flexibility under overfitting; insufficient features and excessive regularization under underfitting.
Iteration count is not a sufficient diagnosis. Held-out performance indicates whether further iterative fitting harms generalization; source wording is conditional, not universal.
Visible four-item enumeration: number of features, regularization strength, dataset size, evaluation strategy. Other plausible optimization choices are not the printed list.
Under fixed data, stable tie handling and no empty clusters, unchanged centers give a fixed assignment/mean-update point. They do not prove globally minimal SSE or initialization independence.
Actual plot title Recompute Centers (3) and triangle legend identify current cluster centers, not initial positions or unseen observations.
Actual task supplies temperature Celsius and Wi-Fi percent, no y labels, requests three clusters. Feature count two does not set k.
Feature-space similarity does not ensure geographic connectedness. Two spatially separated positions may share temperature/Wi-Fi values and hence cluster membership.
Shape (100,2) means 100 sampled rows with temperature then Wi-Fi columns. Neither the two populations nor the distribution parameters occupy those columns.
The actual annotation says standard deviation and code normal(loc,scale,size). These are not bounds; actual plotted purple observations exceed 100 percent.
Legend: exploration circles, red X centroids, magenta star new reading. The star is not the upper centroid or an old training observation.
A consistent bijective renaming of all cluster IDs leaves each equivalence class unchanged, so the partition and objective do not worsen. Independent per-point relabeling can change the partition.
The table gives abnormal torque as a failure-monitoring application, not a proof of a specific mechanical or sensor cause. Anomaly alone requires investigation.
Similar colors can be represented by a smaller palette with possible quantization error. Keeping each original value plus an ID is not that reduction; file overhead remains relevant.
The set of available moves is an action set; left is a selected action, not a state or policy. Source action-definition conflation needs qualification.
Action-reward loop permits stepwise feedback, while the earlier prose illustrates delayed reward. Delays create assignment of credit across earlier actions; not only the last action matters.

Given an action-responsive simulator supplying state and reward, it fulfills the functional environment role. It need not be hardware or contain the agent policy; a fixed unresponsive route log is not the same interaction.

Critic feedback rewards/penalizes action outcomes without necessarily labelling the correct action. Labels are supervised feedback; clustering/reconstruction alone does not define this reward feedback.
Trying a less-known route to learn is exploration; choosing current highest estimated reward for that reward is exploitation.
First summary bullet motivates learning when sensor patterns resist manual rules; final warning requires actual task alignment. Better accuracy for an unrelated target does not repair that mismatch.
Known targets motivate supervised, unlabeled structure unsupervised, and action-dependent reward RL. Continuous input features alone do not turn unlabeled clustering into supervised regression.

np.random.seed controls the global generator used for Gaussian synthetic arrays. The fixed integer KMeans random_state sets estimator randomness separately; it neither regenerates data nor merely fixes semantic group IDs. Extra global draws should not advance the estimator generator when data and integer random_state are fixed.
